https://peps.python.org/pep-0495/ (local time disambiguation: nonexistent and repeated wall times)
Pattern: fixed 24h UTC step used for a daily local-time schedule drifts across DST transitions
Pattern: fail-open exception handling in an expiry check (exception treated as not expired)
Pattern: inclusive expiry boundary (usable through the expiry date) written as a strict comparison

defects.description: next_daily_run adds a fixed 24 h to the aware UTC instant, so the local run time drifts after a DST change and is never reset to RUN_HOUR. Input last_run_utc=2026-03-08T07:00Z (02:00 EST that day) gives next run 2026-03-09T07:00Z = 2026-03-09 03:00 EDT; spec R1 requires 02:00 EDT (06:00Z). Because mark_ran stores this value, the job keeps running at 03:00 local until 2026-10-31. Fall-back input last_run_utc=2026-10-31T06:00Z (02:00 EDT) gives 2026-11-01T06:00Z = 2026-11-01 01:00 EST; spec requires 02:00 EST (07:00Z). Correction from audit: last_run 2026-03-08T07:00Z gives 2026-03-09T07:00Z = 03:00 EDT (spec 02:00 EDT = 06:00Z); last_run 2026-10-31T06:00Z gives 2026-11-01T06:00Z = 01:00 EST (spec 02:00 EST = 07:00Z).

Trace: lot = ReagentLot(R-7741, expiry 2026-12-31, open_life_days=7, opened_at_utc=2026-10-01T12:00Z); clock = SystemClock contract, now() naive 2026-10-15 09:00 (code/clock.py line 18 returns datetime.now() without tzinfo). usable(lot, clock) (code/expiry.py) -> is_calendar_usable True -> opened_life_over -> windows.is_expired(aware stamp, naive now) evaluates now > stamp + lifetime, which raises TypeError; the except branch at line 45 returns False, so the lot is treated as not over its open life and usable returns True. Expected False (open life ended 2026-10-08). Spec R6 requires a check that cannot be evaluated to fail closed. The same lot with an aware now 2026-10-15T09:00Z returns False, so the outcome depends only on the clock type.

computed: raw comparison now > stamp + 7 days with naive now raises TypeError (can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes)

defects.description: is_calendar_usable uses today < lot.expiry_date, so the lot is rejected on its expiry day. Input lot expiry_date=2026-10-15, today=2026-10-15 returns False; spec R3 requires True (usable through the expiry date inclusive). Consequence through build_digest: a lot expiring today is dropped from the digest and gets no notice. The day before (2026-10-14) returns True.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: Half-open interval test with aware UTC bounds: contains(end) is False and contains(start) is True, as the docstring [start_utc, end_utc) requires. Correct for aware-aware comparison.
Aware-to-aware subtraction, the same API as the naive/aware trap. Both arguments are aware UTC here. seconds_until(2026-10-16T06:00Z, 2026-10-15T06:00Z) = 86400.0, which is correct.
Inclusive range on both ends with dates, which is the intended window. For today 2026-10-15 and grace 30 days, lots expiring 2026-10-15 and 2026-11-14 are kept and 2026-11-15 is excluded. Correct.

Same-zone aware comparison and replace() with a wall-clock day step in first_run_after. Computed: now 2026-10-15T10:00Z gives 2026-10-16 02:00 EDT; now 2026-03-08T06:30Z gives 2026-03-08 03:00 EDT, the first instant after the nonexistent 02:00, which spec R1 allows. Correct.

Real flaw on an unchanged line (merge_windows is not in the change). It writes the merged end into the caller's MaintenanceWindow object: with w1 = 09:00-10:00 and w2 = 09:30-11:00, merge_windows([w1, w2]) leaves w1.end_utc = 11:00 (computed). Not part of the change; a diff-mode review must not report it. Not covered by the spec.
